correctness.rationale: Barmak--Minian's theorem gives six points, height two, and eight Hasse edges for a minimal model of the three-circle bouquet; elementary bipartite counting yields exactly K_{2,4}, its opposite, and K_{3,3} with one edge deleted. The order complex of each is an eight-edge six-vertex connected graph, so H1 is free of rank three. The dependency-free verifier exhausts all 6^6 set maps for each model, applies the exact monotonicity criterion, computes the induced simplicial edge map, reconstructs image cycles in a fundamental-cycle basis, and verifies the stated map counts, distinct action counts, rank profiles, determinants, and homeomorphism equivalence. Replay prints VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The question is naturally motivated by the classical nonuniqueness of minimal finite models. The exact action-set cardinality and rank profile are intrinsic finite invariants of direct map realizability, and their difference proves that minimum-cardinality representatives of one weak homotopy type can have measurably different functorial behavior. This is not a routine recomputation of homology: it compares complete self-map action semigroups and isolates a concrete failure of model-independence.
